newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - S-E-Banken to double '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S-E-Banken to double '96 profit.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken was expected to post a 116 percent surge in pre-tax profit after credit losses in calendar 1996 to 5.68 billion crowns, a Reuters poll of 13 analysts found on Monday.
Forecasts varied between 5.29 and 6.04 billion crowns.
The result after credit losses for the first nine months was 4.42 billion crowns.
In 1995 the bank posted a pre-tax profit after credit losses of 2.63 billion crowns. Credit losses were 4.03 billion crowns.
In 1996 credit losses were expected to reach 1.6 billion crowns which led analysts to forecast a result before credit losses of 7.3 billion crowns on average.
Analysts were expecting the bank to propose a dividend of 2.30 crowns a share compared to 1.50 crowns a year earlier.
For 1997 and 1998 the bank was expected to post a profit after credit losses of 5.2 billion and 5.1 billion crowns respectively.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Carnegie, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Enskilda, Fiba, Handelsbanken, J.P. Morgan, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Morgan Stanley, Penser, Swedbank, and Ohman.
S-E-Banken was expected to publish its 1996 earnings on February 14.
